turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mr. Krishnan, good morning. Come, sit. What brings you in today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I have been troubled by a cough, and I thought I should not neglect it.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Of course. Tell me how this cough has been for you.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It is quite dry, doctor. There is no phlegm whatsoever. It has been going on for about three weeks.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): About three weeks. And through the day, or at a particular time?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): More so in the evenings, and when I lie down to sleep. In the office it is milder, though people have remarked on it.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I had connected it to a cold. My wife had one around the same time, so I assumed I had caught the same.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): How did that cold feel, for you personally?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): There was a little blockage in the nose for a couple of days. That has cleared. I did not have fever.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any sore throat with it?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. The throat has been fine.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): And breathlessness, chest pain, any wheeze when you cough?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): None of those, I am glad to say. I manage the two flights at home without stopping.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): That is reassuring. May I ask about your pressure tablets? What are you on just now?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I have had high blood pressure for many years, doctor. I have taken amlodipine, five milligrams, once daily. Then, last month, the clinic near my office added ramipril.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ramipril. And the dose they settled on?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): This is where I am a little unsure, doctor. The nurse there told me five milligrams, once each morning. But the strip I was handed says two point five milligrams. I have been taking the printed dose, one tablet after breakfast, as I did not like to guess.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): So you heard five, and you have actually been taking two point five. We will not pretend those are the same.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. Kindly advise me which is correct. I have the strip in my bag if you wish to see it.

[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please, if it is not a trouble. Yes, the foil says ramipril two point five milligrams. The nurse's note in the referral says five milligrams. I cannot tell from here which was intended.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. I will continue as you direct.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Before I decide, when did the cough begin, relative to starting the ramipril?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I would say the cough came on about a week after I began the new tablet. At first I ignored it.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): And you linked it to the cold, not to the tablet.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Precisely, doctor. A cold seemed the ordinary explanation.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any heartburn, or swelling of the feet? I am just thinking aloud.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No heartburn. The feet are as usual. Um, one more thing, if I may. My elder brother takes lisinopril for his blood pressure, and he coughs a good deal, so I wondered whether these tablets are of one family.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): They are, yes. Lisinopril, ramipril, that group can tickle a dry cough in some people. Your brother's medicine is his own, of course. We will not copy it.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly. I only mentioned it for your information.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you allergic to any medicine, as far as you know?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. No allergies that I am aware of.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or did you?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. I take a small coffee in the office, nothing else of note. I work as an accounts officer, mostly sitting.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me check your pressure while we talk. It is 148 over 92, and the pulse is 76, regular.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): At home on Sunday it was lower, doctor, something like 130 over 80. I use a small machine.

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Home readings often sit a little lower. We will keep both in mind. My first thought is to bring the ramipril up to five milligrams, as the nurse said, and to give you a simple cough syrup for a week, since you feel it is a cold.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): If that is your advice, doctor, I will follow it. Though the cough has already lasted three weeks, and the cold feelings have gone.

[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hmm. You are right to press me on that. Let me reconsider. A dry cough starting a week after ramipril, with the cold symptoms already settled — I would rather not increase an ACE inhibitor that may be the trigger.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): So the syrup is not required?
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): No. I am setting that plan aside. We will stop the ramipril from today, so please do not take another tablet of it.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): In its place I will start telmisartan, forty milligrams, once each morning. You should continue the amlodipine five milligrams as before.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Telmisartan, forty milligrams, with the amlodipine. And ramipril to be stopped entirely. Have I understood correctly?
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): You have. Take the telmisartan after breakfast, same as you did with the ramipril. If you feel dizzy on standing, sit down and ring the clinic.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): I shall do so. May I ask, is the cough then from the ramipril, or from the cold?

[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): It could be either. The timing makes me suspect the ramipril, but a lingering cold can do the same, and I am not going to name it firmly today. We will watch what the cough does once the ramipril is out.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): That is fair, doctor. I appreciate your candour.

[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back in two weeks, whether the cough has eased or not, and we will recheck the pressure. If you become very short of breath, or the cough turns wet with fever before then, do not wait, come sooner.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. I will book it at the desk. Thank you, doctor. Good day.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good day, Mr. Krishnan. Take care.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
